description: A Junior CS major with a background in game engine development and a research interest in ML infrastructure who is highly proficient in C but seeks deeper theoretical insight into concurrency.

nodes.description: Introduction to OS services, system calls, and the fundamental distinction between user and kernel modes.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong_prior_exposure, we move directly into core architectural requirements while skipping introductory scaffolding.
nodes.title: OS Foundations & System Structure

nodes.description: Deep dive into the performance trade-offs between monolithic kernels, microkernels, and hybrid structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong_prior_exposure, exploring structural design trade-offs provides higher-level system insight than basic definitions.
nodes.title: Advanced Kernel Architecture Analysis

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core requirement builds on the student's strong_prior_exposure to ensure theoretical mastery of process abstractions.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle & IPC Mechanisms
nodes.description: Managing process states, lifecycle, and communication methods including shared memory and message passing.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure allows for advanced investigation into memory consistency models within IPC.
nodes.title: IPC Performance & Consistency Models
nodes.description: Exploring the synchronization and consistency challenges in high-performance shared memory systems.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Focuses on the implementation details of threading, leveraging the student's strong_prior_exposure to C/systems code.
nodes.title: Threads & Threading Models
nodes.description: Overview of threading models (User vs Kernel) and standard threading libraries like Pthreads.
Analysis of CPU scheduling algorithms including Round Robin, Priority, and Multi-level Queue scheduling.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core scheduling theory is required for all students; this builds on existing systems knowledge for this strong_prior_exposure student.

nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment covering Chapters 1 through 5 in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required assessment checkpoint to validate the student's strong_prior_exposure against course-specific exam criteria.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Foundations & Scheduling

nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure students need to master these primitives for complex project deliveries later in the course.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives
nodes.description: Solving the critical section problem using mutexes, semaphores, and monitors.
Analysis of lock-free data structures and the challenges of hardware-level atomicity.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Student's strong_prior_exposure enables exploration of advanced lock-free techniques beyond the standard core curriculum.
nodes.title: Advanced Synchronization & Lock-Free Design

nodes.description: Characterization, prevention, and the Banker’s Algorithm for deadlock avoidance.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization & Prevention
nodes.personalizationRationale: Even with strong_prior_exposure, formal deadlock modeling is a mandatory theoretical component for the final exam.

nodes.description: Addressing mechanisms, contiguous allocation, and the transition to paging structures.
nodes.title: Main Memory & Paging
nodes.personalizationRationale: Builds on the student's strong_prior_exposure to explain how physical hardware is abstracted by the OS.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core content for the memory management project, adapted for a student with strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Demand paging, page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO, Optimal), and thrashing.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Enriches the core memory management block by connecting it to modern hardware performance for students with strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Memory Performance & Hardware Interaction
nodes.description: Examination of TLB reach, HugePages, and memory performance optimization in modern architectures.

nodes.title: I/O Systems & Performance
nodes.personalizationRationale: A core capstone topic that integrates hardware and software knowledge for this strong_prior_exposure student.
nodes.description: I/O hardware, polling vs interrupts, and the kernel I/O subsystem performance.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Final mandatory block covering persistent storage, required for the cumulative final exam.
nodes.title: File System Implementation
nodes.description: Structures for file storage, directory implementation, and allocation methods (indexed, linked, contiguous).

nodes.personalizationRationale: A required final assessment to ensure the student with strong_prior_exposure has synthesized all course concepts for the 40% final exam.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review & Assessment
nodes.description: Cumulative review session covering all course material from foundations through file systems.
